questions.question: Which component of the cell organelles principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golgi Apparatus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Golgi Apparatus:

 
 
• The Golgi apparatus has multiple names such as the Golgi complex or Golgi body.
 
• The name is given on the name of the scientist, who discovered the organelle, i.e. Camillo Golgi.
 
• It is found in all eukaryotic cells, plants as well as animals.
 
• They are membrane-bound organelles present in the cytosol of the cell.
 
• The Golgi body comprises 5 to 8-cup-shaped, series of compartments known as cisternae. Cisternae is a flattened, disk-shaped, stacked pouches that make up the Golgi apparatus. A Golgi stack mostly contains 4 to 8 cisternae. However, ~60 cisternae are found in some protists. A mammalian cell contains ~40 to 100 stacks of cisternae.
 
• Animal cells generally contain around 10 to 20 Golgi stacks per cell, which are connected by tubular connections.
 
• The Golgi complex is mostly found near the nucleus.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9501690c5324825b9c437459e780de7351fe3f51e4982825d01d58711e338499.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**.

 
 
• The number of mitochondria in a single cell may be up to 50 to 5000.
 
• The inner lumen of mitochondria contains ribosome phosphate particles and DNA molecules.
 
• It has the potential to synthesize its own protein and oxidation of carbohydrates and fats are taken place with the help of enzymes in mitochondria.
 
• This energy is stored in the form of ATP ( Adenosine Triphosphate ) so, these are known as the "Powerhouse of the cell".​
 
 
 
• Chloroplast:
 
 
• The chloroplast is a double membrane-bound cell organelle.
 
• Out of the two membranes, the inner membrane is relatively less permeable. (the outer membrane contains porins).
 
• The space limited by the inner membrane is called the stroma.
 
• Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments which are responsible for trapping of light energy essential for photosynthesis.
 
• The majority of chloroplasts are found in the mesophyll cells of the leaves.
 
 

 
• **Chromosomes**

 
 
• Chromosomes are thread-like structures located inside the nucleus of animal and plant cells.
 
• Each chromosome is made of protein and a single molecule of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).
 
• Passed from parents to offspring, DNA contains the specific instructions that make each type of living creature unique.

questions.question: Which of the following cell divisions is known as reduction division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis**:-

 
 
• **It is known as reduction division because it reduces the number of chromosomes in a cell by half, resulting in four haploid daughter cells.**
 
• This process is essential for sexual reproduction as it allows for the formation of gametes with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell, which then combine during fertilization to form a zygote with a full set of chromosomes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telophase:-**

 
 
• It is a stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the nuclear membrane reforms around the separated chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
 
 
 
• **Prophase:-**
 
 
• It is the stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis:-**
 
 
• It is a type of cell division where a single cell divides into two identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It does not involve a reduction in chromosome number and is not known as reduction division.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the GO (G zero phase) phase of the cell cycle is most accurate?

options.text: DNA synthesis occurs rapidly in cells present in the GO phase.
It is the phase where cell division is initiated in cancerous cells.
It is a temporary quiescent stage where cells exit the cell cycle.
Cells in GO actively prepare for DNA replication.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a temporary quiescent stage where cells exit the cell cycle.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The GO phase (G zero phase) represents a state of **cell cycle arrest**, where cells exit the active cycle and stop dividing.
 
• Cells in the GO phase are in a **non-proliferative or quiescent state**, often performing specialized functions depending on the cell type.
 
• This phase is **temporary or permanent**, depending on the cell type and environmental conditions.
 
• Examples of cells in permanent GO phase include **neurons and skeletal muscle cells**, which do not divide after differentiation.
 
• GO phase is crucial for **maintaining cellular homeostasis** and protecting against uncontrolled cell division.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Cycle Phases:**

 
 
• The cell cycle consists of interphase (G1, S, G2 phases) and mitotic phase (M phase).
 
• GO phase is not part of the active cycle and is considered a resting state.
 
 
 
• **Quiescence vs Senescence:**
 
 
• Quiescence refers to reversible cell cycle arrest (GO phase).
 
• Senescence is an irreversible state of cell cycle arrest caused by damage or aging.
 
 
 
• **Role in Cancer:**
 
 
• Cancerous cells often evade GO phase, leading to uncontrolled division and tumor formation.
 
• Targeting the mechanisms regulating GO phase is a focus in cancer therapy research.
 
 
 
• **Cell Types:**
 
 
• Stem cells can exit GO phase to re-enter the cycle and divide.
 
• Terminally differentiated cells like neurons remain in GO phase permanently.

 i) Cell membrane

 b. An important site of formation of glycolipids and glycoproteins
 
 

 iii) Golgi apparatus
 c. Synthesis of lipid
 
 

 iv) Ribosomes
 d. Transport of the molecules
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• i. **Cell membrane** is responsible for **transport of molecules** (Matching with "d").
 
• ii. **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** plays a key role in **lipid synthesis** (Matching with "c").
 
• iii. **Golgi apparatus** is an **important site for the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids** (Matching with "b").
 
• iv. **Ribosomes** are the primary sites for **protein synthesis** (Matching with "a").

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell membrane:**

 
 
• It is a semi-permeable membrane that surrounds the cell, regulating the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• The cell membrane is composed of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.
 
 
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER):**
 
 
• SER is primarily involved in lipid and steroid hormone synthesis.
 
• It also plays a role in detoxification of harmful substances in liver cells.
 
 
 
• **Golgi apparatus:**
 
 
• It processes, packages, and distributes molecules such as proteins and lipids received from the Endoplasmic Reticulum.
 
• It is essential for the modification of proteins into glycoproteins and lipids into glycolipids.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes:**
 
 
• Ribosomes are cellular structures composed of RNA and proteins.
 
• They are the sites of translation where mRNA is used to synthesize proteins.
 
• Ribosomes can be free-floating in the cytoplasm or attached to the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER).

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.text: Mitochondria: Power house of the cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus: Lipid metabolism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The nucleus is the control center of the cell, storing the cell's DNA and coordinating cellular activities such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• Lipid metabolism is primarily associated with the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and not the nucleus.
 
• The nucleus is responsible for the transcription of DNA to mRNA, which is then translated into proteins by ribosomes.
 
• The nucleus also contains the nucleolus, which is involved in ribosome synthesis and assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lysosomes:**

 
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes to break down biomolecules.
 
• They are often referred to as the "suicidal bags" of the cell because they can digest cellular components when the cell is damaged.
 
• They play a key role in the degradation and recycling of cellular waste, cellular signaling, and energy metabolism.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses of the cell" because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are involved in other processes such as signaling, cellular differentiation, and cell death, as well as the control of the cell cycle and cell growth.
 
• Mitochondria have their own DNA and are thought to have originated from ancestral prokaryotes through endosymbiosis.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes:**
 
 
• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• They translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into amino acid sequences to build proteins.
 
• Ribosomes can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or bound to the endoplasmic reticulum, forming the rough ER.
 
• They are made up of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins and consist of two subunits, a large and a small one.

questions.question: Which scientist explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudolf Virchow.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Rudolf Virchow expanded the cell theory and suggested that **all the cells arise from pre-existing cells.**
 
• The cell theory, given by **Rudolf Virchow in 1855**, states that:
 
 
• All living organisms are made up of cells.
 
• The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
 
• All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Theodore Schwann**

 
• He was a **British Zoologist who in 1839, studied different types of animal cells.**
 
• On the basis of this, Schwann proposed the hypothesis that the bodies of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells.

**Anton Van Leeuwenhoek**

 
• He is known as **"the Father of Microbiology"**.
 
• He discovered "protozoa" - the single-celled organisms. 

**Robert Hooke**

 
• **He discovered cells by observing them in a cork slice** in 1665.
 
• Under a microscope, he could only see honey- comb-like structures in a slice of cork.
 
• Since that was a dead tissue, he could only see the cell walls.
 
• **He thus coined the term ‘Cell’.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Mitochondria is INCORRECT?

options.text: ATP generating chemical reactions get enhanced by the deeply folded surface area of the mitochondria.
The body uses energy stored in ATP for making new chemical compounds and for mechanical work.
Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mitochondria are indeed capable of making their own proteins.** They contain their own DNA and ribosomes which allow them to synthesize certain proteins independently.
 
• The mitochondrial inner membrane is extensively folded into structures known as cristae, which increase the surface area available for ATP-generating chemical reactions.
 
• The energy stored in ATP is used by the body for various processes, including the synthesis of new chemical compounds and mechanical work.
 
• **Mitochondria have a double-membrane structure.** The outer membrane is smooth, while the inner membrane is folded into cristae.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are unique in having their own genome, which is similar to bacterial genomes, and they reproduce independently of the cell in which they reside.
 
• The double-membrane structure of mitochondria consists of an outer membrane and a highly convoluted inner membrane, the latter being the site of the electron transport chain and ATP synthesis.
 
• The inner membrane folds over many times to create layered structures called cristae. The increased surface area of these cristae enhances the mitochondrion's ability to produce ATP.
 
 
 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**
 
 
• ATP is the energy currency of the cell, providing the energy needed for many biochemical cellular processes including muscle contraction and protein synthesis.
 
• It is produced primarily in the mitochondria through a process known as oxidative phosphorylation, which occurs along the inner mitochondrial membrane.
 
 
 
• **Protein Synthesis in Mitochondria**
 
 
• Mitochondria have their own ribosomes and DNA, which enable them to produce some of their own proteins independently of the cell's nuclear DNA.
 
• The mitochondrial DNA encodes for a small number of proteins essential for the organelle’s function, particularly those involved in the electron transport chain.

__
 
• A** Golgi body, also known as a Golgi apparatus,** is a cell organelle that helps process and package proteins and lipid molecules, especially proteins destined to be exported from the cell.
 
• **Named after its discoverer, Camillo Golgi, the Golgi body appears as a series of stacked membranes.**
 
• The **Golgi is located right near the nucleus.**
 
• The Golgi body is a portion of the cell that's made up of membranes.

**Vacuoles :**

 
• A vacuole is a membrane-bound cell organelle.
 
• In animal cells, vacuoles are generally small and help sequester waste products. 
 
• In plant cells, vacuoles help maintain water balance.

**Lysosomes :**

 
• Lysosomes function as the digestive system of the cell. 
 
• A lysosome has three main functions: the breakdown/digestion of macromolecules (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids), 
 
• Cell membrane repairs, and 
 
• Responses against foreign substances such as bacteria, viruses and other antigens.

**Mitochondria :**

 
• Mitochondria play an essential role in creating energy to drive cellular function and basically all of our biological processes. 
 
• It is called Power House of the Cell. 
 
• Chemical energy produced by the mitochondria is stored in a small molecule called adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

questions.question: Which of the following is not a function of cytoskeleton in a cell?

options.text: Maintenance of cell shape and structure

questions.solution:
**__Concept__****:**

__
 
• **Cells **are the structural and functional unit of life.
 
• They exist in different shapes and sizes.
 
• The **structure of a cell** is directly proportional to its function.

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• A **cytoskeleton** is found in the **cytoplasm as a network of protein filaments**.
 
• There are three types of cytoskeletons found in the cytoplasm- **microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments. **
 
• They are found only in eukaryotic cells.
 
• Cytoskeleton **provides mechanical support to the cell** and helps maintain the shape of the cell.
 
• They are important for **cell division and movements inside the cell.**
 
• They also function in supporting **the cell organelle** and allow cell motility.
 
• **Intracellular transport** is not carried out by the cytoskeleton.
 
• There are **vesicles and certain motor proteins **that help in intracellular transport.

So, the correct answer is **option i.e. Intracellular transport**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** **Microtubules, Microfilaments, and intermediate filaments are proteinaceous structures to support the extensive system of membranes that collectively form the cytoskeleton of a cell.
 
• The microtubules occur in cilia, flagella, centrioles and basal bodies, mitotic apparatus, etc.
 
• The microfilaments are mainly composed of the globular protein actin but have filamentous protein myosin also.
 
• Microfilaments are involved in cytoplasmic streaming and amoeboid movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **cell wall** provides structural strength and rigidity to plant cells, protecting them from mechanical damage and pathogens.
 
• **Ribosomes** are the sites of protein synthesis in the cell, translating genetic information into proteins essential for various cellular functions.
 
• **Lysosomes** are involved in breaking down and digesting foreign materials, cellular debris, and worn-out organelles, functioning as the cell's waste disposal system.
 
• The **Golgi apparatus** is involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles, and it is linked to the production of lysosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Wall**

 
 
• Found in plants, fungi, and certain prokaryotes, but not in animal cells.
 
• Made primarily of cellulose in plants, chitin in fungi, and peptidoglycan in bacteria.
 
• Provides structural support and protection, and helps maintain cell shape.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes**
 
 
• Composed of ribosomal RNA and proteins.
 
• Can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum, forming rough ER.
 
• Essential for translating mRNA into polypeptide chains during protein synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**
 
 
• Contain hydrolytic enzymes capable of breaking down various biomolecules.
 
• Play a key role in cellular homeostasis and recycling processes.
 
• Involved in processes such as autophagy, where the cell digests its own components to recycle nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**
 
 
• Consists of a series of flattened membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.
 
• Involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins and lipids.
 
• Works closely with the endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for transporting macromolecules within the cell.

questions.question: Eukaryotic cells are much more complex as compared to prokaryotes. Which one of the following structures is exclusively present in a eukaryotic cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria **are membrane-bound organelles found exclusively in eukaryotic cells.

 
 
• They play a crucial role in cellular respiration, producing energy (ATP) for the cell.
 
• **Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria**.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** mitochondria, as it is a eukaryotic-specific organelle not found in prokaryotic cells**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell wall:**

 
 
• **​**Both **eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells** can have a cell wall.
 
• In prokaryotes, such as bacteria, the cell wall is composed of peptidoglycan.
 
• In eukaryotes, plant cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, and fungi have a cell wall made of chitin. 
 
 
 
• **Plasma membrane:**
 
 
• **Both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells** have a plasma membrane, which is a lipid bilayer that surrounds the cell and controls the passage of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• It is a fundamental structure in all types of cells.
 
 
 
• **Nucleic acid:**
 
 
• **Nucleic acids, specifically DNA, are found in both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells**.
 
• However, the organization and location of the genetic material differ between the two cell types.
 
• Eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus that houses their DNA, while prokaryotic cells have a nucleoid region where the DNA is located, but it is not enclosed within a membrane.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organ is called "Suicidal Bags"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosomes **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lysosomes are **membrane-bound organelles found in animal cells.**
 
• They are called **"Suicidal Bags"** because they contain digestive enzymes that can break down the cell itself.
 
• These enzymes are capable of degrading all types of **biological polymers – proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.**
 
• **Lysosomes digest excess or worn-out organelles, food particles, and engulfed viruses or bacteria.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 Incorrect term. Possibly a confusion with Endoplasmic Reticulum, which synthesizes and transports proteins and lipids.
 
 

 **2) Stork**
 Not related to cell biology. Possibly a typographical error or misplaced term.
 
 

 **3) Mitochondria**
 Known as the powerhouse of the cell, mitochondria generate the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.

questions.question: The _______ principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**golgi apparatus**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Golgi Bodies Functions:**

__
 
• **Its main function is the packaging and secretion of proteins**.
 
• It receives proteins from Endoplasmic Reticulum. It packages it into membrane-bound vesicles, which are then transported to various destinations, such as lysosomes, plasma membrane or secretion.
 
• **They also take part in the transport of lipids and the formation of lysosomes.**
 
• Post-translational modification and enzymatic processing occur near the membrane surface in Golgi bodies, e.g. phosphorylation, glycosylation, etc.
 
• Golgi apparatus is the site for the synthesis of various glycolipids, sphingomyelin, etc.
 
• **In the plant cells, complex polysaccharides of the cell wall are synthesised in the Golgi apparatus.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Golgi Apparatus:**

 
• The Golgi apparatus has multiple names such as the **Golgi complex or Golgi body.**
 
• The name is given on the **name of the scientist, who discovered the organelle, i.e. Camillo Golgi.**
 
• It is found in **all the eukaryotic cells, plants as well as animals.**
 
• They are membrane-bound organelles present in the cytosol of the cell.
 
• The Golgi body comprises 5 to 8 cup-shaped, series of compartments known as cisternae. Cisternae is a flattened, disk-shaped, stacked pouches that make up the Golgi apparatus. A Golgi stack mostly contains 4 to 8 cisternae. However, ~60 cisternae are found in some protists. A mammalian cell contains ~40 to 100 stacks of cisternae.
 
• Animal cells generally contain around 10 to 20 Golgi stacks per cell, which are connected by tubular connections.
 
• **Golgi complex is mostly found near the nucleus.**

questions.question: Which of the following area pair of barrel-shaped organelles located in the cytoplasm of animal cells near the nuclear envelope, which give orientation to the 'mitotic spindle' formed during cell division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centrioles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Centrioles are a pair of barrel-shaped organelles located in the cytoplasm of animal cells near the nuclear envelope.
 
• They play a crucial role in the organization of the mitotic spindle during cell division.
 
• Each centriole is composed of nine sets of microtubule triplets arranged in a cylindrical form.
 
• Centrioles help in the formation of cilia and flagella, which are structures involved in cell movement and signaling.
 
• During mitosis, centrioles duplicate, and the pairs move to opposite poles of the cell to assist in the segregation of chromosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centrosome**

 
 
• The centrosome is the main microtubule organizing center of the cell and is composed of two centrioles.
 
• It regulates the cell's cytoskeleton and is vital for the integrity of cellular processes.
 
• During cell division, the centrosome duplicates to ensure each daughter cell inherits one centrosome.
 
 
 
• **Mitotic Spindle**
 
 
• The mitotic spindle is a structure composed of microtubules that segregates chromosomes into the daughter cells during mitosis.
 
• Spindle fibers are crucial for the accurate separation of chromosomes.
 
• The spindle apparatus originates from the centrosomes.
 
 
 
• **Microtubules**
 
 
• Microtubules are tubular structures that provide structure and shape to cells.
 
• They are composed of tubulin proteins and are integral to many cellular processes, including vesicle transport and cell division.
 
 
 
• **Cell Division**
 
 
• Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides into two or more daughter cells.
 
• It is essential for growth, reproduction, and repair in multicellular organisms.
 
• There are two types of cell division: mitosis and meiosis.

questions.question: The stage in cell division that consists of G1 phase, S phase,G2 phase is:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Cell Division** is the process by which a mature cell divides and forms 2 nearly equal daughter cells which resemble the parental cell in a number of characteristics.
 
• 2 processes take place during cell reproduction.
 
• **Cell growth:** this is the period of synthesis and duplication of various components of the cell.
 
• **Cell division:** It is the process which a mature cell divides into two cells.
 
• The Cell cycle completes in 2 steps: 

 
• **Interphase**
 
• **M-phase/Dividing phase**

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Interphase **is the period between the end of one cell division to the beginning of the next cell division.
 
• The **interphase takes almost 95% of the total time** of the cell cycle.
 
• During interphase, the cell prepares itself for the next division, and it grows in size. So the **cell is the most active metabolically in Interphase.**
 
• Interphase is divided into 3 phases:

 
• **G1 phase/**Post mitotic/Pre-DNA synthetic phase/Ist gap phase
 
• **S-phase/**Synthetic phase
 
• **G2-phase/**Pre mitotic/Post synthetic phase/IInd gap phase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Earlier Interphase was considered as the **resting phase** in the cell cycle, but recent studies have revealed that the cell is the most active in this phase as it prepares for the next division, **so it cannot be called resting instead it is called the preparing phase.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• M-phase/Dividing phase has four sub-phases: **Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase**

questions.question: Which unicellular organism acquires food by a process in which cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane?

__
 
• In **Amoeba**, the cell membrane help in** engulfing the food **during the process called **endocytosis.**
 
• Amoeba is **a unicellular organism that has the ability to change its shape**.
 
• They are usually found in** water bodies such as ponds, lakes, and slow-moving rivers.**
 
• Sometimes, these **unicellular organisms** can also make their way inside the human body and cause **various illnesses**.
 
• Amoebae do not form a single** taxonomic group; **instead, they are found in every major **lineage of eukaryotic organisms.**** **

• ​Volvox is **a genus of green algae containing around 20 species of freshwater algae**.
